variabel.text: Create the variable `{{nameVar}}` containing your name, and then use `echo` to print `{{hello}}` followed by the name.

substitution.text: Save the number of lines in `~/{{documents}}/server.log` in the variable `{{linesVar}}`, using `$(...)` and `wc -l`.
substitution.hint: `wc -l < file` prints just the number, without the file name: `{{linesVar}}=$(wc -l < ~/{{documents}}/server.log)`

if.text: Write an `if` statement that prints `{{exists}}` if the file `~/.bashrc` exists.
if.hint: `if [ -f ~/.bashrc ]; then echo {{exists}}; fi` – don't forget the spaces inside the square brackets.

for.text: Print the numbers 1 to 5, one per line, with a `for` loop.
for.hint: Either `for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do ...; done` or `for i in $(seq 1 5); do ...; done`.

while-read.text: Read `~/{{documents}}/{{fruits}}` line by line with `while read` and print `{{fruitLabel}}: ` in front of each line.

funktion.text: Create the function `{{doubleFn}}` that prints its first argument times two. Test it with `{{doubleFn}} 21`.

backup.text: Write the script `~/backup.sh`, which copies the file given as the first argument to the same name with `.bak` at the end. Make it executable and run `./backup.sh {{notes}}` in your home directory.
backup.hint: Create the file with `cat > ~/backup.sh << '{{heredocEnd}}'`, write `#!/bin/bash` and `cp "$1" "$1.bak"` on separate lines, and finish with `{{heredocEnd}}`.
